fact: The adult human skeleton has 206 bones; babies are born with around 300, which fuse together as they grow.
title: Bones in the adult human body

fact: The skin is the largest organ of the human body.
title: Largest organ

fact: The liver is the largest internal organ, weighing about 1.5 kg in an adult.
title: Largest internal organ

fact: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone in the human body.
title: Longest bone

fact: The stapes, one of three tiny bones in the middle ear, is the smallest bone in the human body.
title: Smallest bone

fact: The human heart beats about 100,000 times per day, pumping roughly 7,500 litres of blood.
title: Heartbeats per day

fact: A normal resting heart rate for adults is between 60 and 100 beats per minute.
title: Resting heart rate

fact: Normal human body temperature is about 37 degrees Celsius (98.6 F).
title: Normal body temperature

fact: The human brain contains about 86 billion neurons.
title: Brain neurons

fact: The average adult human brain weighs about 1.3 to 1.4 kilograms.
title: Brain weight

fact: Red blood cells carry oxygen around the body using the protein haemoglobin, and unlike most cells they have no nucleus.
title: Red blood cells

fact: Blood makes up about 7 to 8 percent of an adult's body weight.
title: Blood volume

fact: DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) is a double-helix molecule that stores the genetic instructions for building and running the body.
title: DNA

fact: The human genome contains about 3 billion base pairs of DNA and roughly 20,000 protein-coding genes.
title: Human genome size

fact: Stomach acid is strongly acidic, with a pH between about 1.5 and 2, strong enough to digest food and kill many germs.
title: Stomach acid

fact: The small intestine is about 6 metres long in an adult.
title: Small intestine length

fact: The human body has more than 600 muscles.
title: Muscles

fact: Light travels at 299,792,458 metres per second in a vacuum — about 300,000 km/s.
title: Speed of light

fact: Sound travels at about 343 metres per second in air at 20 degrees Celsius.
title: Speed of sound

fact: Einstein's famous equation E=mc^2 says that mass and energy are two forms of the same thing.
title: E=mc^2

fact: Absolute zero, the coldest possible temperature, is -273.15 degrees Celsius (0 kelvin).
title: Absolute zero

fact: Gravity on the Moon is about one-sixth of Earth's gravity.
title: Gravity on the Moon

fact: Pure water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at standard atmospheric pressure (1 atm).
title: Water boils

fact: Pure water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius at standard atmospheric pressure.
title: Water freezes

fact: Ice floats on water because water expands when it freezes, making ice less dense than liquid water.
title: Ice floats

fact: Diamond is the hardest known natural material, rated 10 on the Mohs hardness scale.
title: Diamond hardness

fact: Gold's chemical symbol is Au, from the Latin word 'aurum'.
title: Gold's symbol

fact: The periodic table contains 118 known chemical elements.
title: Periodic table size

fact: Plants use photosynthesis to convert carbon dioxide, water and sunlight into glucose and oxygen.
title: Photosynthesis

fact: About 71 percent of Earth's surface is covered by water.
title: Water coverage

fact: Earth's atmosphere is about 78 percent nitrogen and 21 percent oxygen.
title: Atmosphere composition

fact: Earth takes about 365.25 days to orbit the Sun once.
title: Year length

fact: Earth rotates once on its axis in about 24 hours.
title: Day length

fact: The Moon is about 384,400 km from Earth on average.
title: Distance to the Moon

fact: The Sun is about 150 million km from Earth (one astronomical unit).
title: Distance to the Sun

fact: The Sun's diameter is about 109 times Earth's diameter.
title: Sun's size

fact: One light-year is about 9.46 trillion kilometres.
title: Light-year

fact: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system.
title: Largest planet

fact: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.
title: Closest planet to the Sun

fact: Venus is the hottest planet, with surface temperatures around 465 degrees Celsius, due to a runaway greenhouse effect.
title: Hottest planet

fact: Olympus Mons on Mars, about 22 km high, is the tallest known volcano in the solar system.
title: Tallest volcano

fact: A day on Venus (243 Earth days) is longer than its year (225 Earth days), and it spins backwards.
title: Venus day vs year

fact: A lightning bolt can reach about 30,000 degrees Celsius — roughly five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
title: Lightning heat

fact: Neptune has the fastest winds in the solar system, reaching about 2,100 km/h.
title: Neptune's winds
